key_insight: StreamingQEC turns fault-tolerant quantum error correction into a resource-aware streaming pipeline, making system-level bottlenecks visible during logical execution.
engineering_relevance: It helps architects size controllers, decoders, accelerators, and communication links for tightly integrated quantum-classical systems under realistic QEC timing constraints.
method: Discrete-event simulator as the reference execution model
Automatic staged-fluid approximation for faster design-space exploration
Certified recurrence to reuse repeated transitions only when scheduling state and metrics match
evidence_signal: The paper reports a decoder-runtime dataset of 9,998 measurements, validates recurrence across 35 calibrated configurations, and shows 24.0x speedup on a 16-job workload while preserving 59,743,936 decoding events.
watch_item: Approximate staged-fluid results can deviate from explicit simulation, so accuracy should be checked when QEC cadences, workloads, or resource contention patterns change.
paper_title: StreamingQEC: Streaming Quantum Error Correction in Tightly Integrated Quantum-Classical Systems via Certified Recurrence
